---
title: CLI
---

Run the installed command through uv:

```sh
uv run restic-backups
```

In an interactive terminal, running without a command opens a described
arrow-key menu for **Jobs**, **Repositories**, and configuration validation.
Choose a job before choosing run, status, snapshots, advanced restic, or its
type-specific tools. Explicit subcommands remain available for scripts and
scheduled jobs.

Every menu level includes **Help** and **Back**. **Help** shows the commands and
flags for the current level, then returns to the same menu; it does not load the
configuration or contact remote storage.

Press Escape to return to the previous menu. Press Ctrl+C at any prompt to exit
the TUI cleanly.

Show command-line help instead:

```sh
uv run restic-backups --help
```

Commands that use a repository require a configuration file. Pass the global
options before the command:

```sh
uv run restic-backups --config config.yaml generic repository list
uv run restic-backups --config config.sops.yaml --sops job list
```

The equivalent environment variables are `RESTIC_BACKUPS_CONFIG` and
`RESTIC_BACKUPS_SOPS=1`. See [Configuration](configuration.qmd) for setup.

Commands use standard Python stderr logging with local ISO 8601 timestamps,
levels, and logger names. Add `--verbose` before the command, or set
`RESTIC_BACKUPS_VERBOSE=1`, to include command-level details without printing
credentials or repository passwords:

```sh
uv run restic-backups --verbose generic repository init
```

## Prometheus metrics

Jobs can push their latest result to a Prometheus Pushgateway. Set its URL before
running a job:

```sh
export RESTIC_BACKUPS_PROMETHEUS_PUSHGATEWAY_URL=http://pushgateway:9091
uv run restic-backups job run photos
```

The pushed gauges report the last run timestamp, duration, overall success, and
success per destination repository. They are grouped by hostname and job ID and
labelled with the job type and whether the run was a dry run. Metrics are
disabled when the environment variable is unset. A failed push is logged as a
warning and does not change the backup result.

| Metric | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `restic_backups_job_last_run_timestamp_seconds` | Completion time |
| `restic_backups_job_last_run_duration_seconds` | Run duration |
| `restic_backups_job_last_run_success` | Overall result (`1` or `0`) |
| `restic_backups_job_repository_success` | Result for each destination (`1` or `0`) |

## Audit log

Command auditing is enabled by default. `restic-backups` appends compact JSON
objects to `audit-log.json` in the directory where it was started. Each command
has two linked records:

- a `started` event containing an `id`, `start-time`, `hostname`, `command`, and
  its exact `args`;
- a `finished` event containing `started-id`, `end-time`, and `successful`.
  Workflows may also add non-secret component and destination results under
  `details`.

The `started-id` links completion to the corresponding `started` event. A
`started` event without a matching `finished` event indicates an interrupted
process. The file is append-only: existing records are never rewritten. It is
created with owner-only permissions (`0600`).
Interactive selections are recorded when run, and restic subprocess records
contain the exact raw restic arguments, including generated repository options.
GitHub repository jobs likewise record every raw `git`, `git lfs`, `gh`, and
`restic` command.
Credentials and repository passwords are passed through the environment rather
than arguments. Values attached to password-, secret-, token-, credential-, and
key-like arguments are replaced with `[REDACTED]`.

The log can still reveal repository names and local paths. Keep it private and
rotate or archive it according to your own retention policy. To turn auditing
off explicitly:

```sh
export RESTIC_BACKUPS_AUDIT=0
```

The values `false`, `no`, and `off` are also accepted, case-insensitively.

## Root commands

| Command | Purpose | Repository access |
|---|---|---|
| `check-config` | Load and validate configuration | No |
| `job ...` | List, run, and inspect every configured job type | Depends on subcommand |
| `generic ...` | Run generic configured repository commands | Depends on subcommand |
| `github-repository ...` | Compatibility and GitHub-specific commands | Depends on subcommand |
| `voice-memos ...` | Compatibility and Voice Memos-specific tools | Depends on subcommand |

Use [Generic Backups](generic.qmd) for restic passthrough, repository
initialization, restores, and managed data directories. Use
[GitHub Repositories](github-repositories.qmd) for Git history and selected
GitHub-hosted data. Use
[Voice Memos Backups](voice-memos.qmd) for the macOS-specific workflow.

Run subcommand help without loading a configuration:

```sh
uv run restic-backups job --help
uv run restic-backups generic --help
uv run restic-backups github-repository --help
uv run restic-backups voice-memos --help
```
